extracted.intended_audience: prospective nonfiction authors and literary agents submitting book proposals to Storey Publishing (gardening, crafts, homesteading, nature, cookbooks, children’s activity books, etc.)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and submitting a complete nonfiction book proposal to Storey Publishing, specifying required proposal components, editorial fit, market/comparative analysis, and publicity expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with Storey mission and publishing areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The books we select to carry out our mission include nonfiction titles for adults and children in the areas of gardening, herbs, cooking, beer & wine, nature, farming, animals, building, homesteading, natural health, home reference, crafts, and mind/body/spirit. We encourage you to take a close look at Storey’s publishing program on our website before submitting a proposal to ensure that your work fits within the areas we publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your topic and approach align with Storey’s stated mission of publishing practical information that encourages personal independence in harmony with the environment. Review Storey’s existing publishing program to confirm topical fit before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit fiction
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not currently publish fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only nonfiction proposals in the listed subject areas will be considered; fiction submissions are inappropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letter of introduction
rubrics_metrics.description: A letter of introduction summarizing succinctly the topic of your proposed book, your reason and credentials for writing the book, and why you think the book would be appropriate for Storey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the letter concise but informative—state topic, unique angle, and your qualifications; explain why Storey is the right home for the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-paragraph book description
rubrics_metrics.description: A one-paragraph description of your book idea focused on what makes it unique, intriguing, and necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This should be a tight, compelling elevator-pitch style description emphasizing uniqueness and necessity to hook the editor quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed table of contents with chapter descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed table of contents, including a brief description of what will be covered in each chapter and proposed projects or recipe lists (if appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide chapter-by-chapter summaries that show structure, scope, and concrete content; include sample projects/recipes when relevant to demonstrate practical value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Craft books: photographs of finished projects
rubrics_metrics.description: For craft books: please send photos of a selection of finished projects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include high-quality images that demonstrate the aesthetic and achievable results of projects to show visual appeal and execution level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Children’s activity books: sample chapter
rubrics_metrics.description: For children’s activity books: please send a complete sample chapter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a full chapter to demonstrate tone, educational/activity design, layout, and child-appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format, length, and production considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Your thoughts about the length, format, photographic and illustrative requirements, suggested packaging, and general appearance of the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe expected trim/page count, visuals (photo vs. illustration), packaging or special features, and any production considerations that affect cost or market positioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship: experience and credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: A detailed summary of your experience and credentials for writing the book you are proposing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document relevant professional background, subject-matter expertise, prior publications, teaching or practical experience that establishes authority to write the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing samples
rubrics_metrics.description: Samples of your writing from previous books, magazines, or online publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include representative work that demonstrates voice, clarity, and suitability for the proposed audience; prior published work is preferred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publicity and marketing plan
rubrics_metrics.description: A proposed publicity plan detailing your ability to promote and sell your book, including: stats for your online platform and following (Facebook, Instagram, website readership, etc); connections with key media partners, publications, and organizations that would help promote your book; teaching and speaking venues where you are known; noted individuals you are connected with who would potentially endorse and help promote your book; availability and commitment to travel and promote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide measurable data (follower counts, website traffic), named media/organizational contacts, a plan for appearances/teaching, and clearly state your willingness/ability to travel for promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Market statement (target readers and channels)
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief statement describing the potential readers of the book and the channels where you think your book would sell. Who will buy this book and why? Please be as specific as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define demographic and psychographic reader profiles, likely retail/online channels, and specific reasons these readers will purchase the book (needs, gaps, trends).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative books analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of comparative books with similarities to your proposed book (in content or approach) that have been published within the last three years (include title, author, page count, retail price, and publisher). Please add your own critique of each book and how your proposed book differs or complements each one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete bibliographic details for each comparable title and an analytical comparison that shows market positioning and differentiation. Note: similar books can indicate a strong market rather than being a negative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address proposal to appropriate editor
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use the list below to choose the appropriate editor. Send via email to: storey_submissions@hbgusa.com (Editors listed with subject areas: Carleen Madigan: gardening; homesteading; self-sufficiency; farming; herbal health. Hannah Fries: science and nature (both adult and kids); literary anthologies; building. Gwen Hawkes: cookbooks; crafts; home reference. Kristen Hewitt: nature; health/wellness; creativity/mindfulness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the editor whose subject areas most closely match your book and address the proposal accordingly; use the provided submission email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Response timeframe and volume note
rubrics_metrics.description: Given the volume of submissions, we regret to say that we cannot respond to every inquiry. If we are interested in a proposal, we will respond within 6-8 weeks of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect that many submissions will not receive individualized replies; follow up only after allowing the stated response window to pass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission sources and contract terms
rubrics_metrics.description: We are always pleased to review proposals submitted directly from authors and from agents. We offer standard royalty contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both direct author submissions and agented submissions are accepted; compensation is via standard royalty contracts (no alternative deal structures specified here).
